findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is a public service-provider interface, and making `order()` abstract breaks source compatibility for every existing third-party implementation. More importantly, an older implementation can still be discovered at runtime, but the new sorting code invokes `order()` on it and gets `AbstractMethodError`, preventing crypto-provider initialization. Give the method a default priority to preserve compatibility, or otherwise provide a migration path that does not fail during discovery.

findings.title: Equal-priority providers leave FIPS selection dependent on discovery order
findings.body: The built-in `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider`, and `FIPS1402Provider` all return priority 200. The comparator therefore does not distinguish them, and the stable sort preserves ServiceLoader enumeration order; when multiple providers are present, whichever is discovered first is selected, with no guarantee that the FIPS provider wins. A classpath containing both FIPS and non-FIPS providers can consequently initialize with non-FIPS cryptography despite the FIPS provider being available. Assign distinct priorities or reject ambiguous top-priority providers.
